ex.en: I had a weird feeling that someone was watching me.
ex.zh: 我有一种奇怪的感觉，好像有人在看着我。

words.note: weird 口语常用，比 strange 更强调怪得离谱，常修饰感觉、声音。

ex.en: The region is characterized by hot summers and mild winters.
ex.zh: 该地区的特点是夏季炎热、冬季温和。

words.note: characterize 多用被动 be characterized by 表以…为特征。

ex.en: The plane began its descent towards the runway.
ex.zh: 飞机开始向跑道下降。

words.note: descent 是 descend 的名词；别与 decent（得体的）混淆。

ex.en: It seemed ridiculous to worry about such a small problem.
ex.zh: 为这么小的问题担心似乎很可笑。

words.note: ridiculous 语气较强，口语常用；动词 ridicule 表“嘲笑”。

ex.en: The country went through a turbulent period of political change.
ex.zh: 这个国家经历了一段政治变革的动荡时期。

words.note: turbulent 源自“搅动”，可形容时局、气流和水流。

ex.en: There was no overt conflict between the two departments.
ex.zh: 两个部门之间没有公开的冲突。

words.note: overt 与 covert（隐蔽的）相对，多形容态度或行为。

ex.en: The lawyer used new evidence to refute the accusation.
ex.zh: 律师用新证据驳倒了这项指控。

words.note: refute 强调用证据驳倒；表示“拒绝”的是 refuse，勿混。

ex.en: The court's decision set a precedent for similar cases.
ex.zh: 法院的判决为类似案件开了先例。

words.note: set a precedent 是高频搭配，precedent 重音在第一个音节。

ex.en: The drought caused a severe shortage of drinking water.
ex.zh: 干旱造成饮用水严重短缺。

words.note: severe 比 serious 更强调严厉或严酷的程度。

ex.en: New details about the accident emerged during the investigation.
ex.zh: 调查过程中出现了有关这起事故的新细节。

words.note: emerge 后接 from 表来源，emerge as 表最终成为某种角色。

ex.en: Her early paintings exemplify the spirit of the movement.
ex.zh: 她早期的画作体现了这场运动的精神。

words.note: exemplify 是 example 的同源动词，指“作为…的典型”。

ex.en: They signed a three-year lease on the apartment.
ex.zh: 他们签下了这套公寓的三年租约。

words.note: lease 多指房屋、土地的租约；合同到期说 the lease expires。

ex.en: The company was accused of exploiting its workers.
ex.zh: 这家公司被指控剥削工人。

words.note: exploit 一词两义：开发资源与剥削他人，注意结合语境。

ex.en: She slapped him in the face and walked away.
ex.zh: 她打了他一记耳光，然后走开了。

words.note: slap 表示掌击；a slap on the wrist 指象征性的轻罚。

ex.en: They celebrated their tenth wedding anniversary with a small party.
ex.zh: 他们办了个小型聚会庆祝结婚十周年。

words.note: anniversary 前用序数词，如 tenth anniversary。

ex.en: You must register for the exam before the end of the month.
ex.zh: 你必须在月底前报名参加考试。

words.note: register for 后接活动，register with 后接机构。

ex.en: Good managers communicate clearly with their teams every day.
ex.zh: 优秀的管理者每天都与团队进行清晰的沟通。

words.note: communicate with sb 表“与某人交流”，比 talk 正式。

ex.en: There is little evidence to support his claim.
ex.zh: 几乎没有证据支持他的说法。

words.note: evidence 不可数，说 a piece of evidence，不加 -s。

ex.en: The old train started with a sudden jerk.
ex.zh: 那列旧火车猛地一颠，开动了。

words.note: jerk 指猛地一动，口语中也可指“讨厌的家伙”。

ex.en: He tends to fling his clothes onto the floor.
ex.zh: 他总把衣服随手扔在地板上。

words.note: fling 强调用力扔，过去式和过去分词都是 flung。

ex.en: The news of his resignation stunned his colleagues.
ex.zh: 他辞职的消息让同事们大为震惊。

words.note: stun 表“使震惊”，形容词 stunning 则表“极美的”。

ex.en: Acid rain has damaged many forests in the region.
ex.zh: 酸雨已经损害了该地区的许多森林。

words.note: acid 作形容词还表“尖刻的”，如 acid remarks。

ex.en: The new law gives local governments greater autonomy.
ex.zh: 新法律赋予地方政府更大的自主权。

words.note: autonomy 由 auto（自己）加 nom（法则）构成，即自治。

ex.en: The transmission of the disease was slowed by travel bans.
ex.zh: 旅行禁令减缓了这种疾病的传播。

words.note: transmission 是 transmit 的名词，可指信号、疾病或权力的传递。

ex.en: She blushed when everyone turned to look at her.
ex.zh: 大家都转头看她时，她脸红了。

words.note: blush 指因害羞脸红；flush 多指因激动或饮酒脸红。

ex.en: I am dubious about the accuracy of these figures.
ex.zh: 我怀疑这些数字的准确性。

words.note: dubious 后接 about 表怀疑，比 doubtful 更正式。

ex.en: Her intuition told her that something was wrong.
ex.zh: 她的直觉告诉她出事了。

words.note: intuition 常加 a；形容词 intuitive 表“直觉的”。

ex.en: Artillery fire could be heard from the front line.
ex.zh: 前线传来炮火声。

words.note: artillery 是不可数集合名词，常作定语修饰 fire。

ex.en: The government promised to reform the educational system.
ex.zh: 政府承诺改革教育体制。

words.note: educational 指“与教育有关的”，educated 指“受过教育的”。

ex.en: Climate change poses a serious threat to coastal cities.
ex.zh: 气候变化对沿海城市构成严重威胁。

words.note: pose a threat/risk 是高频搭配，不表示“提出威胁”。
